sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closest to H. luzonensis from the Philippines; it differs in the slightly stouter nasus, the less distinct rostral hump and the wider posterior part of the head.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark brown except the vertex; vertex, antennae, palpi, thoracic and abdominal tergites and legs brown; apex of the nasus, ventral surface of the abdomen, trochanters and tibial joints light brown. Cephalic setae few: 2 on the vertex, 2 at the base of the nasus, 1—2 on the nasus; tergites with fine, scattered setae; sternites with long setae, mostly posterolaterally. Posterior part of the head broadly oval; in lateral view moderately concave, with a slight rostral hump. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 4. Mandibles pointed. Pronotum nearly 1.5 times as wide as long, with a pale longitudinal stripe extending to the meso- and metanotum; pronotal angles rounded. Measurements (mm; 10 specimens, range / mean): head length including nasus 1.80—1.98/1.93; head width 1.17—1.25/1.22; nasus length 0.63—0.73/0.68; pronotal length 0.40—0.44/0.42; pronotal width 0.64—0.70/0.68.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality: Strickland River, Papua, 1928-7-31, several soldiers and workers (C. E. Pemberton). Fig. 4: A head in dorsal view, B pronotum, C head in lateral view. The original describes only the soldier, not the worker or the alate.

note: Rewritten from the species-level description on pp. 4–5 of New Termites, American Museum Novitates 1344 (15 April 1947), the original in English. The archive.org identifier given in the source pack, dli.ernet.28272, has the title "New Termites (Indian Zoological Memoirs / 1947)", which does not match the running head of the text (AMERICAN MUSEUM NOVITATES, No. 1344); the author's name does not appear in the pack (to be verified). The pronotal width is printed in the original as "'0.64-0.70" (an extra single quotation mark, OCR noise); the figures are reproduced unchanged. From line 124 of the pack the text is the new species Hospitalitermes moluccanus, which was not used.
